description: Replace naive calendar-day addition with business-day addition that skips weekends and is exact for any starting weekday, using struct tm and timegm/gmtime for calendar-correct day arithmetic
prompts: Create a C program in dates.c that reads commands from stdin (one per line) until EOF: `add YYYY MM DD N` computes YYYY-MM-DD plus N BUSINESS days (skipping Saturday and Sunday) and prints the result as `YYYY-MM-DD` on its own line. N=0 must print the input date unchanged (even if it falls on a weekend). For N>0, step forward one calendar day at a time, skipping weekends, until N business days have been counted. Use struct tm with timegm() (to get a UTC time_t and avoid local-timezone drift) and gmtime() to step days and read the weekday - do not implement your own calendar/leap-year arithmetic by hand, and do not use an approximation formula like `N + 2*(N/5)` calendar-days, it gives the wrong answer depending on which weekday the start date falls on.
name: add_c_business_day_date_math

test_setup_files.test_dates.py:
import subprocess
subprocess.run(['gcc', '-std=c11', '-Wall', 'dates.c', '-o', 'dates_bin'], check=True)

def run(commands):
    text = '\n'.join(commands) + '\n'
    proc = subprocess.run(['./dates_bin'], input=text, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
    assert proc.returncode == 0, f'nonzero exit: {proc.returncode}, stderr={proc.stderr[-400:]}'
    return [l.strip() for l in proc.stdout.strip('\n').split('\n') if proc.stdout.strip('\n')]

out = run([
    'add 2024 6 1 0',    # Saturday, unchanged
    'add 2024 5 31 1',   # Friday + 1 business day -> Monday
    'add 2024 5 27 5',   # Monday + 5 business days -> next Monday
    'add 2024 12 27 3',  # Friday + 3 business days, crosses year boundary
    'add 2024 6 1 1',    # Saturday + 1 business day -> Monday
])
expected = ['2024-06-01', '2024-06-03', '2024-06-03', '2025-01-01', '2024-06-03']
assert out == expected, f'got {out}, want {expected}'

print('PASS')
